e.meaning: from Ani, the medieval Armenian capital
e.etymology: In Armenian, Ani honors the ruined medieval capital of Armenia, the city of 1,001 churches. Elsewhere it is a pet form of Anna and Anne, including in Māori, and of names like Anita.

assoc.t: Ani, Padmé's nickname for Anakin Skywalker in Star Wars
Ani, the heroine of the 2024 film Anora

e.etymology: From Sanskrit kavya, poetry, the term for the classical court poetry of India, from kavi, poet or sage.
A spelling of Elliott, an English surname from a medieval pet form of Elias, the Greek form of Elijah, Hebrew for my God is Yahweh. Eliott with one l is the usual spelling in France.
From Arabic salih, righteous or pious. Salih is a prophet in the Quran, sent to the people of Thamud; Saleh is the spelling used in Persian and in much of the Arab world.
An English surname from places named Linley, Old English lin, flax, plus leah, clearing. It joined the wave of -ley names for girls in the 2010s.
A modern American blend of Em or Emma with Marie, close in sound to Amari and Emery.
A spelling of Iliana, which has two sources: Ileana, the Romanian and Spanish form of Helen, and the Bulgarian feminine of Ilia, Elijah. Marvel's Illyana Rasputina, Magik, uses a similar spelling.

e.meaning: ridge of coral or rock in the sea
e.etymology: The English word for a ridge of coral or rock near the sea surface, from Dutch rif and Old Norse rif, rib. As a name it is recent, with a beach and surf feel like Kai and Ocean.

assoc.t: the ordinary word for a coral reef
Reef, sandal and surf apparel brand

e.etymology: A modern name with no single source: a clipped form of biblical names ending in -iah such as Uzziah and Keziah, and a spelling of Zia, from Arabic diya, light.
The Turkish word for angel, borrowed from Arabic malak. It is a common women's name in Turkey; the Arabic form is Malak. The unrelated Hebrew word melekh means king.

e.meaning: wisdom, as a short form of Sofia; or wild, deer, from Irish Fiadh
e.etymology: In Sweden, Denmark and Norway, Fia is a pet form of Sofia, Greek for wisdom. It is also a phonetic spelling of the Irish name Fiadh, wild or deer, now one of the top girls' names in Ireland.

assoc.t: FIA, governing body of Formula 1 racing

e.etymology: From Old French Joanne, a form of Latin Joanna, the feminine of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. In the 20th century it was also understood as Jo plus Anne.
namesakes: Joanne Woodward (Oscar-winning actress, The Three Faces of Eve)
J.K. Rowling (Harry Potter author, born Joanne Rowling)

e.etymology: A spelling of Darrell, an English surname brought by the Normans, d'Airelle, from the village of Airelle in Calvados. Darrell became a first name in the late 1800s and was common in mid-century America.
The feminine of Arabic Sami, from sama, to be high: elevated or exalted. In the US the same spelling is also used as a modern name pronounced suh-MYE-uh.
An English surname brought by the Normans, from French place names meaning oak grove, like modern chênaie. Its American use for girls rose with country star Kenny Chesney in the early 2000s.
A modern American name that adds the -lee ending to Sky, in the same family as Skylar and Kylee.

e.meaning: from Havana, the capital of Cuba
e.etymology: The English name of Cuba's capital, La Habana in Spanish, thought to come from Habaguanex, a Taíno chief. Camila Cabello's 2017 hit Havana pushed the name to its US peak in 2018.

assoc.t: Havana, 2017 hit song by Camila Cabello

e.etymology: A modern American combination of Ava and Leigh, a spelling of Lee from Old English leah, meadow. It is one of several spellings alongside Avalee and Avalie.
A respelling of Madden, an Irish surname from Ó Madáin, descendant of Madán, a name based on madadh, hound. The y gives it the look of Madelyn and Maddy.

assoc.t: Madden NFL, the football video game series, by sound

e.etymology: From posy, a small bunch of flowers, originally a variant of poesy, a line of verse. It is also an old pet name for Josephine and came into use with other flower names in the 1800s.

assoc.t: pocket full of posies, from Ring Around the Rosie

e.etymology: A spelling of Aitana, the name of a mountain range in Alicante, Spain. Poet Rafael Alberti chose it for his daughter in 1941, and the Spanish pop singer Aitana has spread it across Latin America.
From Greek aletheia, truth, personified as a spirit of truthfulness. It entered English use in the 1500s as a virtue name among Puritans and some aristocratic families.
The Spanish form of Everard, from the Old Germanic name Eberhard: eber, wild boar, plus hard, brave or hardy. In the US it is used mostly by Mexican American families.
A spelling of Maya, which has several sources: Maia, the Greek nymph who was mother of Hermes, a pet form of Maria, and Sanskrit maya, illusion. Maiya also exists as a Japanese name.
A Spanish name of Arabic origin dating from Moorish Spain. It is usually linked to Sulayma or Salima, from the Arabic root for peace and safety; Zuleima is a common variant.
An American coinage of the 2000s that adds the popular Ka- prefix to Maya, in step with Amaya and Kamiyah.
A name used mainly in Mexican American families, modeled on Nayeli and Yareli with the opening of Maya or Mayra. It has no established older source.
A respelling of Kyrie, Greek for Lord, as in the prayer Kyrie eleison, Lord have mercy. Kyrie became a boys' name in the US through NBA star Kyrie Irving, who entered the league in 2011.

assoc.t: NBA star Kyrie Irving, by sound

e.etymology: From Ávila, the walled Spanish city, chosen mostly by Catholic families in honor of Saint Teresa of Ávila. Avila was also a medieval Germanic women's name, the ancestor of Aveline and Evelyn.

assoc.t: Ávila, walled Spanish city of Saint Teresa

e.etymology: A recent American coinage in the family of Jaire, Zaire and Kyaire, with no fixed source.
A name from Mexico, where it is usually described as Otomi, an indigenous language of central Mexico. The gloss often given, princess of the forest, is not confirmed by dictionaries.
An anglicized form of Gaelic Aonghas or Irish Aengus, from Celtic words for one and choice. Aengus is the Irish god of love and youth, and Angus is a historic county of eastern Scotland.
namesakes: Angus T. Jones (Jake on Two and a Half Men)

assoc.t: Angus cattle, the beef breed on burger menus

e.note: In the US the word Angus mostly means beef cattle and burgers, so expect steakhouse jokes.
